title: Propagate delegated actor context through the Quest adapter instead of declaring every write human
summary: Propagate delegated actor context through the Quest adapter instead of declaring every write human
description:
Reported from the cli-test review and Orbitfall project exercise on 2026-09-04. Installed tools: Lore 0.4.1 and Quest 0.3.2, macOS ARM64. Source review revisions: Lore 054e6590f1b81fda418c9891611f84fd35aacf6e; Quest dcb06f6520e08f2755c04166cca168318a94ae5a. Findings describe those tested versions, not a claim that current HEAD was retested. Evidence paths below are retained in the sibling cli-test checkout; the reproduction and outcomes are also included here. Filing is not a fix.

Source-confirmed attribution gap: src/adapters/quest.ts defines ACTOR_FLAGS = ["--actor", "lore", "--actor-kind", "human"] and uses them for Quest writes, including adapter migration operations. A delegated caller cannot preserve its declared agent identity and accountable human through this constant.
Reproduce by inspecting/capturing the Quest subprocess argv for a Lore-triggered edit from a delegated-agent session: it declares actor lore, actor-kind human regardless of the caller. The source constant is the direct evidence; this finding does not claim that principal:null proves authorization failure or durable audit loss.
Expected: an explicit supported actor-context input is validated and propagated according to Quest's contract. Human and delegated-agent invocations should remain distinguishable. Related completed work LCLI-407 verifies edit semantics but does not resolve this caller attribution gap.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Lore accepts and validates explicit human or delegated-agent actor context for Quest writes.
Delegated writes pass the agent identity and accountable human instead of hardcoded human attribution.
Adapter tests assert argv for edits and migration paths and verify any promised persisted attribution; missing context fails before writes.
